description: Real-time MCU: ESP32-S3 + onboard QMI8658C 6-axis IMU
package: dev board, on the right-hand key board's rails (PCB-CLUSTER), its pad rows on HDR-MATRIX
notes: Mounted low for acceleration sensitivity. 17 GPIO on its two pad rows (1-7, 33-40, 43, 44) and 12 used. MOUNTED ON THE RIGHT-HAND KEY BOARD (owner, 2026-10-02; ADR 0021 amendment): bare header pins (HDR-MATRIX) join its pad rows to that board's two rails through a shim (MECH-MATRIX-SHIM), four wires (W-MATRIX) its TP2, TP3 and two button pads, and CBL-MCU-RIBBON runs from the board's J-MCU-KB to J-MCU. Its USB-C is the instrument's USB port, by the panel-mount extension to the tail face (mechanical/DESIGN.md); NO ESD ARRAY on that path, by the owner's decision (ADR 0021 amendment 2026-10-02): the Matrix's own D+/D- reach the ESP32-S3 with nothing between [ds WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf, USB block]. Native USB - verified, not a UART bridge - so USB MIDI works. 4MB flash, 2MB QUAD PSRAM, both on-package: the vendor schematic marks U66 = ESP32-S3FH4R2 [datasheets/mechanical/WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf; F=in-package flash, H4=4MB, R2=2MB quad PSRAM from Espressif's ordering code, from memory], so GPIO33-37 are free - octal PSRAM would have taken them. The 8x8 matrix is the instrument's only display, under a window in the top face (ADR 0015) - measure idle draw at E1 to size the shared lighting budget

description: Conformal coating for the in-body boards
notes: Breathed into for hours behind 18 unsealed switch cutouts, interior 10-20K above ambient. MASK BOTH SENSOR PORTS FIRST - a sealed reference chamber gains ~5.2kPa when warm and the output clips at zero, looking like a dead sensor (ADR 0003). THE SENSOR IS SOLDERED TO THE BOARD AND COATED WITH IT: a sensor swap breaks the coating at its eight joints - re-mask both ports before touching it up

part: 4-layer PCB - the main board: thumb switches, both thumb registers and the carrier circuits
description: Thumb switches and their registers, breath sensor, reference, ADC, umbilical, SPI egress, LED drive and the LED row, the regulator, service header
package: long and narrow, sized in mechanical/drc.echo (main board), 1.6mm (config/body.yaml switch.pcb_t)
notes: ONE board at the thumb level, mouth cap to the end of the right hand (ADR 0017). A TONGUE runs on from its tail end to the etherCON's adapter and carries J-UMB, soldered into both (ADR 0021). The thumb switches solder into it; the key boards connect to it by 12-conductor IDC ribbons (CBL-CHAIN), a through-hole right-angle J-CHAIN header for each in its far band beside the LED row. Parts face up - mechanical/drc.echo gives the room under the key boards and elsewhere. A clearance hole for each U-bolt leg, no edge notches, and a plated PWR_GND hole at each mount, every one on the cassette's bottom plate: the stud, the spacer, the board, then a column's standoff or an end mount's nut (ADR 0022, ADR 0025). Its underside faces the grounded bottom plate over its whole length, so an underside part needs a window cut in the plate (hardware/boards/main-board/README.md). 1.6mm, as the key boards, its top pressed against the thumb switches' housing bottom (ADR 0020 Amendment 6). Long: check the board house's panel and price before M4. FOUR LAYERS, signal / ground / power / signal (ADR 0017 amendment 2026-09-29): layer 2 the PWR_GND plane with the analog island, power-entry-instrument.md section 2. WHITE SOLDER MASK, both faces (owner, ADR 0028): the top face is the LED row's first reflector. ASSEMBLY: JLCPCB assembles the parts whose sheet field Assembly is machine (the SMT passives, ICs and the LED row). HAND-SOLDERED, Assembly=hand on the sheets: the thumb switches (SW1-n), the through-hole headers J-CHAIN x2, J-UMB, J-MCU and HDR-SERVICE, the U-BUCK module (THT SIP) and the breath sensor U-BREATH. The Matrix (U-MCU-RT) is on the right-hand key board, not this one: CBL-MCU-RIBBON reaches it from J-MCU

part: 2x12 1.27mm shrouded box header, right-angle, keyed (XKB X1270WR-2x12A-9TV01)
description: The Matrix's connector on the main board: CBL-MCU-RIBBON from the right-hand key board's J-MCU-KB plugs in here, and unplugs with the key plate raised
notes: PART: XKB X1270WR-2x12A-9TV01, LCSC C5147255, through-hole right-angle, keyed and shrouded, all gold flash, 1A per contact [ds connectors/XKB-X1270WR-2x12A-9TV01.pdf]; the sheet carries it, footprint drawn from that drawing (hardware/lib/README.md). Mates the Yxcon IDC3-24232A1AUC1 sockets of CBL-MCU-RIBBON - a standard 1.27mm IDC fit, confirm on the first pair. WHERE: the main board's tail end beside the regulator block, its MOUTH FACING THE TAIL (mechanical/export/pcb-geometry.echo 'J-MCU', direction +1), J-MCU-KB straight above it on the right-hand key board, so the ribbon rises from one socket's back to the other's. PINOUT (ADR 0018), ribbon conductor n = pin n, odd and even across the two rows, pin 1 where XKB's drawing and JLC's footprint put it (hardware/lib/README.md): 1 5V, 2 GND, 3 5V, 4 IO1, 5 IO2 (spare), 6 IO7, 7 IO3 (spare), 8 IO38, 9 GND, 10 IO35, 11 GND, 12 IO36, 13 3V3, 14 IO34, 15 GND, 16 IO39, 17 5V, 18 IO37, 19 IO33, 20 IO40, 21 IO44 (RX), 22 IO43 (TX), 23 IO0, 24 EN. hardware/carrier/netlist.yaml is authoritative. Every fast line - IO35 SCLK, IO36 MOSI, IO34 CS_MOD, IO38 chain SCK, IO7 SH/LD - has a ground, a supply or a static line on both sides; pin 9 is the ground between SCLK (IO35) and the chain clock (IO38). EN is on the edge with only IO0 beside it: the Matrix has no capacitor on EN (R8 10k to 3V3 and Key1 to GND, nothing else - datasheets/mechanical/WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf). IO2 and IO3 are spare and reach no other part on the main board; bring them to two test pads beside J-MCU. KEYED AND SHROUDED: a reversed plug puts 5V on a GPIO. RATING: the 5V and GND contacts carry the whole Matrix draw, and fed from the 5V pad nothing on the Matrix limits it (its USB diode is bypassed - matrix-led-current, power_path), so rate them against U-BUCK's 1A (R-78E5.0-1.0), not against matrix-led-current: three 5V contacts at ~0.33A and four GND at ~0.25A each [calc, equal sharing], against the header's and the socket's 1A per contact [ds XKB-X1270WR-2x12A-9TV01.pdf; YXCON-IDC3-24232A1AUC1-1.27MM-IDC-SOCKET.pdf].

part: 24-way flat ribbon, 0.635mm pitch, with a 2x12 1.27mm IDC socket at each end
description: The Matrix's wiring: J-MCU-KB on the right-hand key board, which carries the Matrix, to J-MCU on the main board
notes: CONDUCTORS: 24, conductor n = J-MCU pin n = J-MCU-KB pin 25-n (J-MCU row; hardware/carrier/netlist.yaml is authoritative, the key board's sheet is held to it by tools/kicad.py check). SOCKETS: two Yxcon IDC3-24232A1AUC1 [ds YXCON-IDC3-24232A1AUC1-1.27MM-IDC-SOCKET.pdf], one each end, keyed. J-MCU-KB is the same header as J-MCU hung upside down from the key board, so the KEY-BOARD SOCKET IS CRIMPED TURNED OVER: its pin 1 on conductor 24, the main-board socket's on conductor 1. Both keys then face their headers' slots and the ribbon runs flat between them with no twist; a socket crimped the other way will not go in. CURRENT: at U-BUCK's 1A (R-78E5.0-1.0) the three 5V conductors carry ~0.33A each and the four GND ~0.25A [calc, equal sharing]; a 0.635mm conductor carries that without heating to speak of [from memory]. RESISTANCE IS WHAT THE FOUR GROUNDS ARE FOR: ~34mohm per 100mm [from memory, ~30AWG], four in parallel ~8.5mohm per 100mm. On the key board the Matrix's grounds join its GND_CHAIN pour, so its return also has the key chain ribbon's five grounds in parallel (hardware/nets.yaml GND_CHAIN). The Matrix's 3V3 is the ADC's reference (carrier/breath-adc) and is regulated against the Matrix's ground, so LED return current in these grounds moves it. E11 confirms it: breath output clean while the matrix is exercised. LENGTH: mechanical/drc.echo 'Matrix ribbon length' between the sockets, the key plate held routing.chain_raise off its columns, as the key chain's; closed it folds flat between J-MCU and the USB-C plug ('Matrix ribbon closed'). A DEAD MATRIX: raise the key plate, unplug J-MCU, desolder the Matrix's pins and wires from the key board, fit the replacement on new pins and shim - nothing on the main board is touched

part: 2x12 1.27mm shrouded box header, right-angle, keyed - the same part as J-MCU
description: The Matrix ribbon's key-board end: CBL-MCU-RIBBON from J-MCU plugs in here, on the right-hand key board's underside
notes: PART: as J-MCU (that row says which, and the sheet's fields carry it). WHERE: hung upside down from the right-hand key board's underside straight above J-MCU, its mouth toward the tail too (mechanical/export/pcb-geometry.echo 'J-MCU-KB'), so the ribbon rises straight from one socket's back to the other's. PINOUT: pin k carries J-MCU pin 25-k (CBL-MCU-RIBBON says why); hardware/boards/key-board-rh/key-board-rh.kicad_sch is held to hardware/carrier/netlist.yaml by tools/kicad.py check. Its tails come up through the key board under the key plate. Assembly: hand

description: The Matrix's two pad rows to the right-hand key board's two rails: bare pins through rail, shim and Matrix
package: 2.54mm pin header strip, carrier slid off
notes: ONE PER PAD ROW, pin 1 at the Matrix's USB-C edge: the 5V..IO1 row and the IO33..RX row [ds WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-pinout.png]; the key board's sheet names each pin for its pad. BUILD: pins through the rail from below, MECH-MATRIX-SHIM over them, the Matrix on, its top face held flat; solder both ends, then CUT THE PINS FLUSH ON THE MATRIX'S TOP FACE AND KEEP THE JOINTS FLAT - the pad rows sit under the oak top, outside the window's opening, with only the shim's clearance (drc.echo 'Matrix shim on the extension's rails'). IO4, IO5 and IO6 reach nothing and are soldered for strength. Pin length: the rail, the shim and the Matrix (config/body.yaml boards.key_board_t, boards.matrix_shim_t, boards.matrix_t) plus what is left under the rail, within the rails' parts layer (boards.cluster_smt_h). Part open: any 2.54mm straight header whose carrier slides off - M4. Assembly: hand

description: The Matrix's pads on neither pad row to the right-hand key board's four wire pads (J5)
notes: FOUR WIRES, each from a pad on the Matrix's back side to its pad on the near rail (the key board's sheet names them): TP2 (VCC_5V) and TP3 (GND), its extension test pads, which share the 5V and ground current with the pad row; EN at Key1 and IO0 at Key2, each on the terminal that goes to its 10k pull-up (R8 for RESET/EN, R10 for IO0), NOT the one on GND - with a meter the right terminal reads ~10k to the 3V3 pad and the wrong one 0 ohm to the GND pad [ds WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf]. Nothing in series on EN or IO0: R8/R10 hold them up, the buttons still work, and whatever drives them from HDR-SERVICE pulls to ground only. Route them through the rails' open middle, clear of the USB-C plug. Assembly: hand

description: Spacer under each of the Matrix's pad rows, between the right-hand key board's rail and the Matrix
package: cut strip, a pad row's length
notes: THICKNESS: config/body.yaml boards.matrix_shim_t, against the gap drc.echo 'Matrix shim on the extension's rails' prints - a little under it, so the Matrix's top stands just under the oak. Width: a pin's pad and a little (the body CAD draws it), so it stays off the Matrix's back-side parts. Any rigid insulating sheet of that thickness serves; FR-4 can be ordered with the key boards [from memory]. Without it the Matrix sits on the rails and drops from the oak, and its pins carry it. Assembly: hand
